subject: Post-call: TTFT & streaming SLOs (FinPay) - next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-04T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: TTFT & streaming SLOs (FinPay) - next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps on the TTFT/streaming SLOs we discussed.

Recap (what we heard):
- Target Time-to-first-token (TTFT): <= 120 ms P95 for single-request interactions (main checkout flow).
- Streaming behavior: real-time transcript UI (SSE or WebSocket). Client wants first token as soon as possible and consistent chunk cadence for smooth typing UX.
- Concurrency/throughput: expected peak concurrency ~250 concurrent live sessions, average request size ~300 tokens, peak qps ~120.
- Acceptable tail: they can tolerate up to 250 ms P99 TTFT for heavy tail, but prefer optimization.

Proposed initial SLOs (draft):
- TTFT: P95 <= 120 ms, P99 <= 250 ms (single-request, 1-2k seq lengths).
- Streaming chunk cadence: <= 150 ms between SSE chunks for first 2 seconds, thereafter allow 200-300 ms depending on chunk size.
- Throughput targets: sustain 120 qps with 250 concurrent sessions at 95th percentile latency targets.
- Graceful fallback: if streaming cannot be maintained at latency SLO, auto-fallback to non-streaming with a clear UI flag (we can provide code snippet).

Next steps (action owners & timing):
1) We’ll send a short SLO proposal + recommended deployment profile (attached: SLO_proposal_v1.pdf). — Aditya (today)
2) FinPay to share representative traffic sample or estimated traffic CSV (we requested finpay_traffic_estimates.xlsx). — Alex (by 2026-03-06)
3) Marissa/Dev to run quick PoC on our Dedicated pool with streaming (SSE) and report TTFT numbers back. — Marissa/Dev (by 2026-03-10)
4) Procurement & legal to coordinate any required contract addendum for streaming SLAs (cc: procurement@finpay.com).

Notes / questions for you:
- Can you confirm whether the UI will use SSE or a persistent WebSocket? That affects chunk framing and keepalive settings.
- Any network constraints (enterprise proxies, TLS deep-inspection) we should know about? If so, share a quick network diagram.

Attaching a short checklist and the draft SLO proposal. Happy to jump on a 30-minute technical sync next week if helpful.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT & streaming SLOs (FinPay) - next steps

Thanks Aditya — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) We plan to use a WebSocket-based streaming channel from the client (browser) to our backend, which then proxies to Redwood. We can consider SSE for simpler fallbacks but prefer WebSocket for low overhead.
2) Network: some of our enterprise customers use corporate proxies that can add 50-100ms. We'll flag that as an environmental caveat. No TLS interception for our production fleet.
3) Traffic sample: attached a filled estimate (also sending to procurement). Expect to have the CSV and a 1-hour pcap of representative load by EOD Friday.

Also, is your fallback suggestion something we can toggle at the edge (we control)? We want the ability to switch streaming behavior without a deploy.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Senior Product Manager, FinPay
alex.chen@finpay.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT & streaming SLOs (FinPay) - next steps

Appreciate the quick reply, Alex. A few notes inline and a small ask for the PoC: 

- WebSocket is fine — our runtime supports both SSE and WebSocket streaming. WebSocket gives lower overhead for bidirectional flows and slightly better chunk cadence control.
- Edge toggle: yes, you can control fallback at your edge — we also support a route-level config that flips to non-streaming output or a smaller chunk size without redeploy. We’ll share the config snippet in the PoC notes.
- Network caveat noted — we'll include a conservative 75 ms network delta when we run the PoC so FinPay sees realistic tails.

PoC ask (to make numbers comparable):
- Please provide a 10-minute representative request trace (timestamps + payload sizes) or the 1-hour pcap you mentioned. If pcap is difficult, a CSV of per-request sizes + inter-arrival times is fine.
- Confirm which browsers/platforms you need to support (Chrome desktop + iOS webview?).

Marissa/Dev — can you run an initial Dedicated pool test with the following parameters?
- Model: open-llm-7b (example)
- Batch config: adaptive (start 16ms window)
- Simulated network latency: +75 ms
- Concurrency: 250 sessions (sustained for 5 minutes)
- Measure: TTFT P50/P95/P99, chunk cadence distribution (median ms between first 5 chunks), and throughput qps.

I’ve attached network_requirements.xlsx with suggested firewall/keepalive settings — Alex if you can confirm corporate proxy behaviors we’ll adjust.

I’ll also open a HubSpot task (link below) and a short DocuSign for the PS addendum so procurement can proceed in parallel.

Thanks,
Aditya

Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT & streaming SLOs (FinPay) - next steps

Looping in Dev for the PoC. Quick notes from a technical POV: 

- Streaming chunk cadence: for a UI that wants near-typing feel we typically aim for first chunk <= 80-120 ms and subsequent chunks 80-200 ms depending on model tokenization. We tune generation params (max_new_tokens per chunk + decode intervals) to hit cadence without creating too-small chunks that hurt throughput.
- TTFT contributors: invocation overhead (HTTP/WSS handshake), model compile/kernel cold starts, KV cache warmup. For PoC we’ll pre-warm instances and pin model version to avoid compile variance.
- Measurement plan: we’ll run 3 x 5-min sustained runs at target concurrency and report P50/P95/P99 for TTFT and chunk inter-arrival percentiles. We’ll include a trace bundle and suggested UI thresholds.

Dev — please start the Dedicated pool run today with the parameters Aditya listed. I’ll compile the results into a short slide deck and share by 2026-03-10.

-Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
